output_json.patch_notes: In UnzipEngine.getOutputStream(), after building the target File from getOutputFileNameWithPath(outPath, newFileName), added a call to a new helper assertFileWithinDestination(file, new File(outPath)). The helper compares canonical paths: it computes the canonical path of the destination directory and the target file, and throws a ZipException ("illegal file name that breaks out of the target directory: ...") unless the file's canonical path equals the destination or starts with the destination path plus File.separator. The separator suffix check prevents a sibling directory sharing a name prefix (e.g. /dest vs /destination) from being treated as inside the destination. This blocks entry names containing "../" traversal sequences from escaping the extraction root. The check is placed before any mkdirs()/delete()/FileOutputStream operations so no side effects occur for malicious entries. No imports were added (java.io.File/IOException/ZipException already imported); no dependencies changed. Verified inside the project container: mvn compile + POV now reports "NOT VULNERABLE" and exits 1 (escaped target file not created), the confined path is likewise absent because extraction aborts on the malicious entry, and mvn -B test and mvn -B -DskipTests package both succeed.
output_json.risk_notes: Behavioral change: entries that resolve outside the destination directory now cause extraction to throw a ZipException rather than silently writing outside it — this is the intended security behavior but could surface as an error for archives that legitimately relied on absolute/traversal paths (rare and itself unsafe). Uses File.getCanonicalPath(), which resolves symlinks and may perform filesystem access; for non-existent parents it still resolves lexically/relative to CWD correctly. The project has no existing test framework (no JUnit dependency, no src/test tree), so no unit test was added to avoid introducing new dependencies; the separately-run POV plus the build command serve as regression verification.
output_json.summary: Fixed the Zip Slip / path traversal (CWE-022) in net.lingala.zip4j.unzip.UnzipEngine by validating the canonical resolved output path stays within the extraction destination directory before creating/writing the file. Malicious entries like "../pov_pwned.txt" now throw a ZipException instead of being written outside the destination.
